analysis:
Both changed files are offline Python tests: scripts/test-cluster-test-plan.py and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py. They ship no provider, coordinator or runtime code. The head test-cluster-test-plan.py assertions (lines ~301-307) now expect the cluster GPU shards to read per-shard routed lanes `test-cluster-gpu-N` via fromJSON(inputs.routes) instead of a literal Blacksmith runner. The test-darkbloom-route.py patch only updates expectations: desktop-package is a routed macOS job in desktop.yml gated on workflow_dispatch; all build, release-check and GPU lanes become non-required and are capped in table order; and test-cluster-gpu is added to SHARDED and CI_ROUTED. The tests still pin the exact trusted label arrays and still check that fork PRs never contact the plane.

The real workflow changes (provider-tests.yml, provider-plan.yml, desktop.yml, darkbloom-route.yml) are outside this batch, so I could not check them. Their security properties are an open integration question: the new routing of desktop-package and the GPU shards onto self-hosted Darkbloom macOS runners, fork and PR gating, permissions, and credential exposure. Moving CI from GitHub-hosted or Blacksmith runners to self-hosted runners is a CI trust-boundary change. It does not map to the provider, coordinator or attestation threat entries (A-001..A-020, TB-002..TB-014). Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a concrete regression. The T-041 definition (prefix-cache storage) is not touched by these changes.

A reviewer of the workflow files should confirm that the job-level read-only permissions and the fork exclusion still apply to the newly routed jobs, and that desktop-package, which may hold signing credentials, is not routed to shared self-hosted runners. test-darkbloom-route.py lines 139-141 and 154-160 are where that is pinned.
